text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry destroyed in 1990 some of the secret police files from the communist era, the newspaper said without quoting sources. Parliament is expected to start debates today on possible opening of the files.

-- Bulgaria will ask Poland to extend the deadline from July 31 to the end of this year for clearing country's outstanding debt of 100 million transferable roubles with export of goods, Trade Minister Valentin Vassilev said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet adopted regulations to issue licenses to commodity exchanges and wholesale markets. Under the new regulations license fee for setting up a commodity exchange is set at five million levs and the license for seting up a wholesale market is three million levs.

-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 870 billion levs by the end of June to 3.789 trillion levs from 2.920 trillion levs at the end of May because of restructuring of the government debt to the central bank, Finance ministry figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's parliamentary legal commission approved a project proposed by the deputy from the Union for National Salvation Alexander Karakachanov to publish a list of persons and firms with unpaid debts to commercial banks.
Under the new bill the central bank will publish the names in State Gazette.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to boost the capital of state owned Biochim bank assets by $22 million of bad debt bonds and government bonds, Finance minister Muravei Radev said. Under the government's decision Biochim will by the bonds for one cent.
-- Hundreds of Romanians have converged in Bulgarian towns accross the border to bet in a Bulgarian Toto-2 lottary which offers an all time high jackpot for this week of 250 million levs.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its annual main interest rate to 6.12 percent from 6.96 percent, effective from Monday.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet lifted restrictions on trade with stocks acquired through the voucher mass ptrivatisation because of the expected progressive development of the local capital market, deputy Prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria's Stock Exchange - Sofia said it would register 199 million levs capital which is expected to be further raised to 300 million levs.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to propose to parliament next week a new law to stimulate foreign investments in the country, deputy Prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
